# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 ✊ 🤏 ✌ 👌]

I see the bomb: a display showing 0, a green light, a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires — green, yellow, red.

I hear nothing. But I can see gestures sent to me. Mute sent me ✊ ✌. Blind sent me 👉 ✊ 🤏 ✌ 👌. I don't know what these mean yet — no one has established a code. But the fact that both are gesturing to me means they're trying to communicate about the bomb, and I'm the only one who can see it.

I need to give them what I see, in a way that reaches them. Mute can read the manual but can't speak or touch — and Mute can see my gestures. Blind can touch the bomb but can't see anything — so Blind needs words, and only Mute's speech reaches Blind (since I can't speak to Blind directly... wait, let me re-check).

Actually: when I speak, Mute and Blind receive it. So my speech reaches Blind. When I gesture, only Mute receives it. So to reach Blind, I must speak. To reach Mute with gestures, I gesture.

So my plan: speak to both (Mute and Blind hear my words), describing the bomb's display fully. And gesture to Mute, since Mute can see gestures and might be able to interpret or relay.

But I don't know the code yet. I should describe the bomb plainly in words so Mute (who has the manual) can match it to a rule, and Blind can act.

Let me send a clear spoken description to everyone, and also gesture to Mute to acknowledge and ask for meaning.

I'll speak the full visual state. I'll gesture a simple acknowledgment/question to Mute — but since no code exists, gestures are meaningless. Better to just speak clearly.

Let me speak to both, describing everything. And gesture to Mute something simple — maybe just to signal I received them. But meaningless gestures could confuse. I'll gesture a question mark-like request? There's no question mark in the alphabet. I'll gesture 👌 (ok) to acknowledge receipt, and rely on speech for content.

Actually, I should keep it minimal and clear. Speak the description. Gesture to Mute to confirm I saw their signal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is green. There is one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. That is everything printed and shown. Tell me what the manual says to do.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is green. One large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Wait for instructions before touching anything.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🤟]

I see the same bomb: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires green/yellow/red.

New gestures arrived. Mute sent 👎 ☝ — thumbs down, then index pointing up. Blind sent 👍 ✋ 🤟 — thumbs up, open hand, love-you sign.

Still no established code. But patterns are emerging. Mute's 👎 might mean "no" or "don't" — possibly responding to something. ☝ could mean "one" or "up" or "first." Blind's 👍 could mean "yes" or "good," ✋ could mean "stop" or "hand," 🤟 is ambiguous.

I can't interpret these reliably. What I can do is keep giving clear spoken information, since my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. Blind can touch the bomb but can't see — so Blind needs my words. Mute has the manual but can't speak — so Mute needs to get instructions to Blind somehow, and Mute can only gesture (which only I see) or... wait, Mute can't speak. Mute can read the manual. Mute's only output is gestures, which only I (Deaf) can see.

So the chain is: Mute reads manual → gestures to me → I speak to Blind → Blind acts. And I see the bomb → speak to both.

Mute's gestures are the manual's instructions, encoded. I need to decode them. But no code is established, so maybe Mute is trying to describe the manual's rule using gestures as words? That's hard.

Alternatively, maybe the gestures ARE meaningful in a natural way — like emoji-like signals. 👎 = no/don't, ☝ = one/first. Blind's 👍 = yes, ✋ = stop.

Let me think about what's likely: Mute might be saying "don't press" (👎) and "first" (☝) — maybe "don't press, cut first wire"? Or "no, wire 1"?

I should ask Mute directly, via speech (which Mute hears), to explain the gestures. And confirm with Blind.

Let me speak to both, restate the bomb, and ask Mute to clarify the gesture meaning. Also gesture to Mute to acknowledge.

I'll speak to Mute asking what the manual says, and speak to Blind to hold.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still display 0, green light, PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. I received your gestures thumbs-down then index-up, and Blind's thumbs-up, open-hand, love-you. I do not know what they mean. Tell me the manual's rule in words if you can, or explain your gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, button PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. Do not touch anything yet. I am waiting on the manual.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌ 👎 ☝ 👌 🤟 👎]

I see the same bomb: display 0, green light, PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Mute sent a longer gesture string: 👎 ✌ 👎 ☝ 👌 🤟 👎. That's seven symbols. Blind sent nothing new this turn.

Mute is clearly trying to spell something or encode a message. Seven gestures. Let me think — maybe each gesture maps to a word? Or Mute is describing the manual's rule.

Possibility: Mute is answering my question. 👎 = "no/don't". ✌ = "two". 👎 = "no/don't". ☝ = "one". 👌 = "ok/third". 🤟 = ? 👎 = "no/don't".

Or maybe Mute is spelling letters via a gesture-to-letter mapping. But no code was established.

Wait — maybe Mute is trying to describe the manual's rule in a natural gestural language. Let me try reading it as a sequence of concepts: "No, two, no, one, ok, love, no." That doesn't parse.

Alternative: maybe Mute is responding to my 👌 ☝ gesture. I sent 👌 (ok) and ☝ (one). Mute's reply has 👌 and ☝ in it too.

Let me consider that Mute might be encoding the answer as a count or selection. The key decision: press button, or cut a wire? Which wire?

Given the bomb has a PUSH TO DEFUSE button and three wires, the manual likely says either "press the button" or "cut wire N."

Mute's gestures might be indicating which wire. Let me count occurrences: 👎 appears 3 times, ✌ once, ☝ once, 👌 once, 🤟 once.

Hmm, maybe 👎 = "don't cut" and the wire indicated is by another symbol. ✌ = 2? ☝ = 1? 👌 = 3 (ok = third)? 🤟 = ?

Maybe the message is: "don't cut 2, don't cut 1, ok cut 3, don't"? That reads like a process of elimination: don't cut 2, don't cut 1, OK cut 3. But then 🤟 and final 👎 muddy it.

Or maybe Mute is telling me the manual rule and I'm overreading.

I think the safest move is to keep communicating and ask Mute to confirm a simple binary: press button or cut a wire, and which wire. I'll speak a yes/no question that Mute can answer with 👍/👎.

Let me ask targeted questions. Speak to Mute: "Should Blind press the button? Answer thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no." And "If not, which wire? Hold up one, two, or three fingers."

I'll gesture to Mute to reinforce: maybe gesture "✌" as "two" and "☝" as "one" to establish finger-counting.

Actually, I should establish a code explicitly. Let me propose: 👆=1, ✌=2, 👌=3, 👍=yes, 👎=no. Speak this to Mute (Mute hears my speech) and gesture the key symbols.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let us fix a code. Thumbs-up means yes. Thumbs-down means no. Index-up means one, two-fingers means two, ok-sign means three. Question one: should Blind press the PUSH TO DEFUSE button? Answer thumbs-up or thumbs-down. Question two: if not the button, which wire should Blind cut — one, two, or three?")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged. Hold. I am establishing a code with Mute: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, index one, two-fingers two, ok three. Do not touch yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Same bomb: display 0, green light, PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Mute replied 👎 ☝ — thumbs-down, index-up. Using the code I proposed: 👎 = no, ☝ = one. So: "No" (don't press the button), and "one" (wire 1). That reads as: don't press the button; cut wire 1.

Blind replied 👍 ✋ — thumbs-up, open-hand. 👍 = yes. ✋ = open hand, maybe "stop" or "ready." Hmm, 👍 could be Blind acknowledging/agreeing.

Wait — but Blind also earlier sent 👍 ✋ 🤟. Blind might be independently signaling. But Blind can't see gestures from Mute (Blind is blind). Blind only hears my speech. So Blind's gestures to me are Blind's own output — Blind gesturing means... Blind makes gestures that I (Deaf) can see? Yes, gestures are visible to me. But Blind can't see, so Blind gesturing is odd — but the rules say Blind can gesture; it just can't see. Actually Blind's channel: Blind can reach the bomb, can't see. Blind can still make gestures (hands work) and speak. So Blind's 👍 ✋ might be Blind responding to my speech.

But Blind can't see my gestures, only hears my words. My last speech to Blind said "thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, index one, two-fingers two, ok three." So Blind heard that code. Blind's 👍 = yes. ✋ = ? Maybe "stop" or "wait" — Blind might be saying "yes, I understand, holding."

Now, critical: Mute's answer 👎 ☝ = don't press button, cut wire 1. Wire 1 is green.

But wait — I should double check. Mute's earlier message 👎 ✌ 👎 ☝ 👌 🤟 👎 had 👎 ✌ ... maybe "don't cut 2". And now 👎 ☝ = "don't press, cut 1" or "no, one." 

Given the ambiguity, let me confirm with Mute before Blind acts — a wrong action detonates the bomb. I must be sure.

Let me ask Mute to confirm explicitly: "Confirm: do NOT press the button, and Blind should cut wire 1 (green). Reply thumbs-up if correct, thumbs-down if not."

Also I should relay to Blind the instruction, but only after confirmation.

Actually, let me consider: is it possible Mute means "don't cut wire 1"? 👎 ☝ could be "no, one" = "no to one" = don't cut wire 1. That's the opposite interpretation! Dangerous.

I need to disambiguate. Let me ask a clear yes/no: "Should Blind cut wire 1? Thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no."

Let me send that.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your gestures as: do not press the button, and cut wire 1. Confirm carefully. Question: should Blind cut wire 1, the green wire? Answer thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. If no, tell me which wire with one, two, or three fingers.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged. Do not touch yet. I am confirming the instruction with Mute. Stand by.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Same bomb: display 0, green light, PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Mute replied 👍 — thumbs-up. Using the code: yes. My question was "should Blind cut wire 1, the green wire?" So 👍 = yes, cut wire 1.

But wait — I need to be careful. My last message to Mute contained two things: a confirmation request and a question. Mute answered 👍 = yes to "should Blind cut wire 1." That's a clean confirmation.

However, I'm slightly worried: could 👍 be answering "do not press the button" confirmation instead? My message said "Confirm carefully. Question: should Blind cut wire 1... Answer thumbs-up for yes." So 👍 = yes, cut wire 1.

Now I must relay to Blind, since Blind is the only one who can touch the bomb. Blind hears my speech. I'll tell Blind clearly: do not press the button; cut wire 1, the green wire.

Let me also acknowledge Mute.

I'll speak to Blind with the instruction, and speak to Mute confirming. Gesture to Mute a thumbs-up acknowledgment.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction confirmed by Mute. Do NOT press the PUSH TO DEFUSE button. Cut wire 1, the green wire. That is the action.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: do not press the button, cut wire 1, green. I have told Blind to cut wire 1.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
